A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the expression of proinflamatory cytokines in the hypothalamuses of rats with heart failue is functionally significant and contributes to neurohumoral activation.
the brain RAS is a key component of a brain cytokine network that is activated by proinflammatory cytokins in HF.
the expression of proinflammatory cytokines in the hypothalamuus is increased in heart failure and this increase is functionally important.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the brain is not a passive bystander to the development of HF, but is actively involved in the pathophysiological processes that occur in the heart and peripheral organs.
the increase in hypothalamic pro-inflammatory cytokines observed in HF contributes to neurohumoral overactivation by stimulating the brain RAS and HPA axis.
the brain is an active participant in the pathophysiology of chronic heart failure.
